card.statement:
Let $e_1,e_2,\dots,$ be a basis of a
vector space $U$, $f_1,f_2,\dots,$ be a
basis of $V$, and $g_1,g_2,\dots$ be a
basis of $W$.

- [(a)] The composition of
a linear mapping ${\mathcal
      A}: U\to V$ and a semilinear
mapping ${\mathcal B}:
      V\dashrightarrow W$ is the
semilinear mapping with
matrix

\begin{equation}
(\mathcal B \mathcal
A)_{ge}=\mathcal B_{gf}
\mathcal A_{fe}
\end{equation}

- [(b)] The composition of
a semilinear mapping
${\mathcal A}:
     U\dashrightarrow V$ and a
linear mapping ${\mathcal B}:
     V\to W$ is the semilinear
mapping with matrix

\begin{equation}
(\mathcal B \mathcal
A)_{ge}=\overline{\mathcal B}_{gf} \mathcal
A_{fe}
\end{equation}
card.label: Lemma 2

paper.title: Cycles of linear and semilinear mappings
paper.abstract: We give a canonical form of matrices of a cycle of linear or semilinear mapping V_1 --- V_2 --- ... --- V_t --- V_1 in which all V_i are complex vector spaces, each line is an arrow ---> or <---, and each arrow denotes a linear or semilinear mapping.
